questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The flyover that __connecting__ the two cities is broken.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"connects". **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The task here is to substitute the underlined phrase **"connecting" **in the sentence **"The flyover that connecting the two cities is broken."**
 
• In this case, the correct option, **"connects", **replaces **"that connecting" **to correct the verb tense and agreement.
 
• The flyover is the subject, and the verb needs to match this subject in the present simple tense, referring to a universal or habitual fact.
 
• **"Connects" **is in the third person singular form of the present simple tense.
 
• We add **"-s" **or **"-es" **at the end of the base form of the verb when the subject is a third person singular noun (he, she, it) or any singular noun.
 
• The flyover plays a connecting role between the two cities.
 
 
• This role is a timeless fact, not limited to a certain period.
 
• The present simple tense is used to express such facts.
 
 
 
• So, **"connects" **refers to the fact that the role of the flyover is to serve as a link between the two cities.
 
• When we say **"The flyover connects the two cities", **it implies that this is the function or purpose of the flyover.
 
• Therefore, the correct form of the sentence is: **"The flyover that connects the two cities is broken." **
 
 
• **​**It conveys that the flyover, which serves the purpose of linking the two cities, is currently in a state of disrepair.
 
 

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 2".**

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate **ANTONYM** of the italicised word in the given sentence.

The *miser* hated spending money.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Spendthrift**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Miser**: A '**miser**' is a person who hoards wealth and spends as little money as possible; they are notoriously stingy. (कंजूस or मितव्ययी)

 
 
• **Example**: "Being a **miser**, he never donated to any charitable cause."
 
 
 
• **Spendthrift**: This term involves the idea of excessive expenditure; it refers to someone who spends money in an extravagant, irresponsible manner. (फिजूलखर्च or अपव्ययी)
 
 
• **Example**: "The lottery winner turned out to be a **spendthrift**, spending all his winnings within a few months."
 
 
 
• Hence, the correct antonym for '**miser**' is '**spendthrift**'.

Therefore, the correct answer is "**Option 1**".

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tightwad**: This term is synonymous with '**miser**,' implying a person who spends as little money as possible. (कंजूस or संकीर्ण). It is not an antonym for the term '**miser**'.
 
• **Scrooge**: A '**scrooge**' is another term equivalent to a '**miser**,' indicating a person who is reluctant to spend money. (कंजूस or लोभी)
 
• **Skinflint**: It's again similar to '**miser**,' suggesting an excessively parsimonious person. (कड़ा कंजूस or लालची). It does not serve as an antonym to '**miser**'.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Wrangle for an ass’s shadow
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Argue over petty issues**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Wrangle for an ass’s shadow**: This idiom comes from an old fable where two men were reported to have quarreled about whether or not the one had the right to the shadow thrown by the ass which the other man had rented.
 
• It now stands as a phrase meaning to argue or dispute over trivial or petty matters.
 
 
• **Example:** "They spent the whole afternoon **wrangling for an ass's shadow**, wasting their time on meaningless details."
 
 
 
• Hence, the correct meaning of the idiom '**wrangle for an ass’s shadow**' is '**argue over petty issues**'.

Therefore, the correct answer is "**Option 3**".

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Losing temper easily**: This phrase, while indicative of a form of conflict, does not fully encapsulate the petty or minor nature of the arguments implied by 'wrangle for an ass’s shadow'.
 
• **Making false allegations**: Although arguments may involve false allegations, this option does not specifically match the idiomatic expression which revolves around trivial or small matters, not necessarily untrue claims.
 
• **Fighting for a just cause**: This represents defending or standing up for something right or fair. However, 'wrangling for an ass’s shadow' is about fruitless or pointless arguments, not noble causes, making it an incorrect choice.
